messages:
amanda: Heads-up — spotted a weird cross-org metric flash on the rollouts page. Flip to canary for org A and a split-second later the quota panel shows numbers for org B. Not sure if UI rendering or backend caching.
raj: Can you repro reliably? steps?
amanda: Yep. Staging, steps: /rollouts -> select canary for org-A -> open 'per-org quota' -> quickly switch org via quick-switch to org-B -> panel flashes B's tokens under A then corrects. Happens 40% of the time for me.
sophie: :eyes: Could be prefetch/affinity state getting reused. We prefetch metrics for the next org sometimes and stick an affinity header — maybe the route cache ignores that header.
mike: Any traces or HARs? My hunch is pipeline-level cache key missing tenant hint, so response for B cached and returned for A during rapid swaps.
amanda: I captured a HAR + trace. HAR snippet:
```
GET /internal/rollout/metrics?org=A HTTP/1.1
Host: internal.api.redwood
X-Org-Prefetch: pref-42
Cookie: session=xyz
```
On a quick switch, you see a subsequent request with `X-Org-Prefetch: pref-99` but the UI renders the first payload because the inproc route cache returned a path+query hit. Router-v2 currently keys cache by path+query+user-id, not by prefetched-org header.
raj: That explains it. The gateway strips X-* headers for CDN normalization by default; internal app cache assumed headers irrelevant. Bad intersection.
ellie: We intentionally strip X-Org from edge responses to avoid leaking to CDN. But internal route cache should be tenant-aware. Do we know which cache served the stale payload — edge or app inproc?
amanda: Inproc router-v2 returned the stale payload (confirmed via logs showing cache_hit=true route_cache, origin=router-v2). Edge not involved for these internal endpoints.
sophie: Proposal: introduce a dedicated header `X-RD-Prefetched-Org` that is whitelisted for internal caches and include it in the route cache key. Also sign it at control plane so we don't accidentally trust arbitrary clients.
mike: Also telemetry: right now we tag metrics by payload.org field. Our traces show `auth_org` != `payload_org` for these mismatches. Emit an event when mismatch occurs: severity=warn, include route, cache_key, auth_org, payload_org.
raj: Agreed. Short-term mitigation: disable caching for `/internal/rollout/metrics` and rollout card endpoints. Long-term: add header to key or include auth org in key.
amanda: I'll prototype a hotfix to invalidate route cache on org-switch events and add a UI banner if auth_org != payload_org ("stale data — refreshing"). I can open a PR today.
ellie: Let's scope the rollback: disable caching on staging immediately, canary config for prod. Also add an automated selenium test that rapidly switches orgs and asserts no cross-org rows.
sophie: Filed RWF-487 in backlog: "rollout card prefetch isolation test". Also we should update docs about which X-RD-* headers are safe for internal routing caches.
deploy-bot: Deployed router-v2:2026.3.1 to staging — watch logs in #eng-oncall.
mike: I'll wire up a telemetry alert: if mismatch-rate > 3/min for more than 1m, page oncall.
amanda: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1122 — changes: include `X-RD-Prefetched-Org` in route cache key; invalidate on org-switch; show banner in rollout card when mismatch detected.
raj: Assigned reviews to @sophie and @mike. Also please add a unit test for cache-key derivation and an e2e for rapid-switch.
ellie: Rapid-switch e2e should also assert that cache headers are not leaked to CDN — ensure edge normalization still strips sensitive headers.
sophie: Nice. After merge let's run a 30m soak on staging and then canary to 10% prod.
amanda: Thanks all — will follow up with PR comments and patch notes.
